main_issue: The group mixes direct archive-entry traversal caused by missing or insufficient destination containment checks with a distinct symlink-following overwrite mechanism that can remain exploitable even after lexical/canonical containment validation. Several assigned cases provide only line anchors, so their membership cannot be confirmed from the supplied evidence.
suggested_guideline: Split archive extraction findings into two review rules. (1) For each untrusted archive entry name, resolve it against the extraction root, normalize/canonicalize it using the intended filesystem semantics, and verify that the resulting target remains contained by that root before creating directories, links, or writing content. Reject traversal, absolute-path, separator-normalization, and prefix-confusion variants. (2) Separately, when extraction can create or encounter symbolic links, ensure later file writes cannot follow an existing or archive-created symlink outside the extraction root; validate link targets and use no-follow or race-safe filesystem operations where available.
split_suggestions: Archive entry name controls a resolved extraction target outside the intended root because containment is absent or incorrectly implemented.
Archive extraction writes through an existing or earlier archive-created symbolic link despite lexical/canonical target containment checks.
evidence_notes: TestNG CVE-2022-4065 directly constructs new File(tempDir, jarEntryName) and copies archive content without normalized-destination containment validation, supporting the direct traversal mechanism.
Plexus Archiver CVE-2018-1002200 directly resolves entryName and writes/creates targets without containment validation, supporting the direct traversal mechanism.

Plexus Archiver CVE-2023-37460 is evidence of a symlink overwrite path: its stated containment check exists, but standard-file extraction can write through a symbolic link. This requires a separate guard from simple canonical-prefix validation.
The one-java-agent, QTIWorks, and Goomph entries contain only materialization/line-anchor provenance rather than source-to-sink evidence; their exact mechanism remains unverified.
The mcpmappingviewer and TJWS2 entries are CWE-22 hunk anchors without trace evidence, so they should be inspected before being treated as support for the stated archive-extraction rule.

The current query is useful for generic path-traversal review but is overly broad because it includes reads, deletes, resource loading, and generic path fragments while the evidenced cases center on archive extraction; it also does not explicitly surface symlink-following extraction behavior.
